rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 and Table 2 - the authors acquired an EO-1 Hyperion image over Mackay (2 April 2002), digitised 142 rust-affected and 159 non-affected sample pixels, computed 40 spectral indices and ran their own discriminant function analysis with a 30% hold-out sample.
rows.notes: The study only shows that Hyperion narrow-band indices (especially the new DWSI indices using the 1660 nm SWIR band) can discriminate sugarcane blocks with moderate-to-high orange rust severity from unaffected blocks (hold-out accuracy up to ~95-97%). It reports no result on farmers taking action, disease control, or prevention of further damage; disease management is only mentioned in the introduction as motivation. Detection is a precondition of the claimed pest-control effect, so Q2 is 'no' and upstream is set. The authors themselves note that early-stage detection was not tested and that water-stressed but non-diseased crops could confound the indices.

notes: Full text appears complete (short Letter, pages 489-498). Single image date, single region, single severity level (rated 4 of 5), single sugarcane variety (Q124).
